hero.headline: Pragmatic Hardware for High-Yield AI
hero.subheadline: We focus on high-utilization hardware (30% GPU / 50% CPU) to ensure maximum profitability and flexible workload handling.

sections.title: Balanced Infrastructure for a Global Market
sections.body: In building Kenya AI Compute, we avoided the trap of chasing 'vanity' top-tier GPUs that often come with low margins and long supply waits. Instead, we have engineered a hybrid server park designed for maximum utilization and rapid ROI. Our fleet is composed of 30% GPU nodes (focused on A100-class and modern AMD Instinct alternatives) for AI training and 3D rendering, and 50% high-core-count CPU nodes (AMD EPYC/Intel Xeon) for the massive demand in inference, edge computing, and decentralized cloud services. This 30/50/20 mix (GPU/CPU/Storage) ensures that we can fulfill the requirements of both the DePIN networks (like Render and Akash) and enterprise clients simultaneously. By utilizing high-performance but cost-effective hardware, we keep our CAPEX within the $14M-$18M range for the server park, allowing us to offer clients pricing that is 40% more affordable than global hyperscalers. Additional context: the project follows a clear rollout roadmap that aligns low-cost energy, infrastructure reliability, and flexible deployment models. sections.title: Server Fleet Configuration
items: GPU Nodes: NVIDIA A100-80GB / L40S and AMD MI250X clusters.
CPU Nodes: Dual-socket AMD EPYC 7003/9004 series for high vCPU density.
RAM: Minimum 512GB DDR4/DDR5 per node for large model inference.
Storage: Direct-attach NVMe Gen4 for ultra-fast data access.
Interconnect: Dual 100G NICs per node with RDMA support.
